messages:
alice.prod: quick sync — we're building a 'Cache effectiveness' dashboard for KV + prefix caches. want consensus on the minimal metric set and labels we need from runtime and infra. cc @dmitri.telemetry @eva.data
ben_r: +1. we should be pragmatic: hit/miss counters, evictions, reuse_by_workload, and maybe latency percentiles for cache lookup path.
carla-sre: agree on the list. question: do we expose absolute counters (per-tenant) or rates? cardinality explosion risk if we label by route/model/tenant all at once.
dmitri.telemetry: suggested minimal schema:
```
# counters (monotonic)
kv_cache_hits_total{tenant,route,model,seq_len_bucket} 123
kv_cache_misses_total{tenant,route,model,seq_len_bucket} 45
kv_cache_evictions_total{tenant,route,model,reason}

# gauges
kv_cache_size_bytes{pool}
prefix_cache_reuse_ratio{tenant,route,model} 0.78

# histograms for lookup latency
kv_cache_lookup_seconds_bucket{le,tenant,route} ...
```
we can compute hit rate as rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) / (rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) + rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m]))
eva.data: important: reuse_by_workload needs consistent workload labels. we should standardize on 'workload' where workload = route_name | model_family | pipeline (small set), not freeform route. this reduces cardinality. also add sampled top keys to help debug "hot prefixes" (sampled logs, not metrics).
alice.prod: good point @eva.data. proposal: labels = {tenant, workload, model_family, seq_len_bucket}. seq_len_bucket = one of [0-64,65-256,256+]. keeps cardinality bounded.
ben_r: for evictions we probably want reason label: {capacity, ttl, manual, shard_rebalance}. evictions spike patterns matter.
carla-sre: also add a boolean gauge 'kv_cache_prefix_cached' per-request? that might be high-cardinality. instead we could emit a low-rate log event for cache miss + key fingerprint for samples.
dmitri.telemetry: agree. emit per-request metrics with only low-cardinality labels. For troubleshooting, emit an event stream to S3 with sampled items (1/1000) including key fingerprint, tenant, workload, routing decision.
eva.data: dashboard panels I suggest:
- overall hit rate (cluster) 1h/24h
- hit rate by workload (top 20)
- evictions by reason over time
- reuse ratio distribution by model_family
- hot prefixes (from sampled events)
- lookup latency p50/p95
- per-tenant anomalies (alert if hit_rate drop > 15% vs baseline)

ben_r: quick PromQL examples to include in dashboard config: 
```
# cluster hit rate 5m
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) + rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m]))

# hit rate by workload
sum by (workload)(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum by (workload)(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) + rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m]))
```
alice.prod: how about sampling for heavy workloads to keep series count manageable? e.g. only surface top-N workloads by qps on UI and have a picker to query others.
eva.data: UI UX: default to cluster + top 10 workloads. add 'compare to baseline' toggle (7d avg). also provide a 'show keys' link that leads to sampled events view (S3/ML flow).
dmitri.telemetry: instrumentation tasks for runtime: (1) add counters/gauges above, (2) ensure labels use stable enums (workload/model_family/seq_len_bucket), (3) add histogram for lookup latency, (4) add tag for route_version for rollout experiments.
carla-sre: rollout UX note: when we A/B roll a new cache policy, we need side-by-side panels or label route_version so we can slice hit rate by variant. also add an alert if evictions increase by >x%.
ben_r: internal API debate: do we expose prefix cache reuse as a derived metric (computed in grafana) or compute it in runtime and export as gauge? Runtime computing is slightly cheaper (one division per interval) but adds more exported series. I lean runtime computed 'prefix_cache_reuse_ratio' with same labels as hits/misses to avoid repeated queries in dashboards.
dmitri.telemetry: runtime computed is fine if we keep labels small. otherwise Grafana compute is ok. we'll decide per metric.
alice.prod: ownership & next steps: dmitri + ben to draft metric spec PR (instrumentation + labels) by EOD Tue. eva to mock dashboard panels and prometheus queries by Wed. carla to propose alert thresholds and runbook. I'll schedule 30m sync Thurs to finalize.
deploy-bot: deploy:metrics-collector/202-apply succeeded in 2m 14s :rocket:
ben_r: thanks all — I'll open the PR and ping the runtime owners for review. :thumbsup:
eva.data: I'll start a mock dashboard + sample queries in grafana playground. we should keep the initial dashboard focused so it's actionable.
carla-sre: adding task to incident runbook: how to fallback routing policy if cache hit rate collapses (route to fallback model variant).
alice.prod: perfect. if anyone has edge cases (eg. multi-tenant shared pools) add to the PR comments. otherwise we'll reconvene on Thurs. :calendar:
